note: Hand-picked recent AI reporting from large, reputable newsrooms, links verified. Source mix is limited by access tooling: WSJ, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg are blocked from automated browsing, so the openable/verified set skews CNBC, AP (wire) and MIT Technology Review. The updater (8×/day) can broaden sources over time.

items.title: The Download: Better bionic hands and AI's natural-gas boom
items.blurb: Natural gas is becoming the default way to meet surging US power demand from AI data centers.

items.title: Global stocks rally as investors shrug off U.S. tariffs and AI jitters to 'fish for bargains'
items.blurb: Asian tech shares rebounded after a November slide driven by AI bubble fears and Nvidia's leadership turmoil.

items.title: Beware higher correlation but nab high U.S. credit yields, fund managers say
items.blurb: Fund managers warn AI-linked assets now move together, raising risk if the AI trade turns.

items.title: Cookbook GPT: When AI becomes a Thanksgiving sous-chef
items.blurb: A survey finds 27% of US Thanksgiving celebrants used generative AI for planning or cooking, up from 22%.

items.title: Nvidia chip buyers told to rule out Chinese renters to purchase GPUs, sources say
items.blurb: Chip sellers are reportedly refusing Nvidia supply to cloud providers that rent capacity to Chinese firms, after a Commerce rule took effect Nov 19.

items.title: Robots could be doing household chores in just 1-2 years, Chinese EV firm says
items.blurb: Xpeng says its humanoid robots could handle household chores within one to two years, a bet on AI moving into physical work.

items.title: S&P warns Nvidia credit rating could be cut over 'rising' management and governance risk
items.blurb: S&P put Nvidia's AA rating on watch for a cut, citing board independence, key-man risk and China controls.

items.title: AI debt worries grow as Nvidia rebound masks Big Tech spending squeeze
items.blurb: Investors are questioning how the AI buildout is financed, with industry borrowing estimates ranging from $300 billion to $570 billion.

items.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia return shows the U.S.-China AI race is about more than chips
items.blurb: Huang's return as Nvidia CEO highlights competition between the U.S. and China for AI talent, not just hardware.

items.title: Tech rout deepens globally; Softbank falls 15%, Nvidia down 4.5% premarket
items.blurb: Renewed doubts about the AI trade hit chip and tech stocks worldwide, with SoftBank and Asian chipmakers falling hard.

items.title: Anthropic's stock has been a clunker post-IPO. Why that matters for the AI trade
items.blurb: Anthropic trades below its $83 IPO price, a weight on the wider AI trade and on OpenAI's future fundraising.

items.title: Kalshi traders say the odds of states imposing data center moratoriums is more likely than not
items.blurb: Traders now see state pauses on data center construction as more likely than not, a growing risk to the AI buildout.

items.title: JPMorgan says the S&P 500 will rise to 8,200 next year because of the AI supercycle
items.blurb: JPMorgan argues AI spending remains intact and will lift stocks through 2027, despite the current sell-off.

items.title: What bonds are telling us about the AI trade
items.blurb: Bond investors are growing wary of heavy AI borrowing, a signal stock markets may be underpricing.

items.title: Wes Moore links Washington's AI inaction to corruption and dark money
items.blurb: Maryland's governor says federal inaction on AI leaves Americans exposed, pointing to industry money in politics.

items.title: How I use AI: Airbnb CTO Ahmad Al-Dahle
items.blurb: Airbnb has not ruled out blocking outside AI agents, saying user trust and safety come first.

items.title: Anthropic CEO pushes back on Axios reporting on AI and free will
items.blurb: Dario Amodei rejected the idea that people should hand decision-making to AI, amid a widening split among AI executives.

items.title: Trump open to pardoning Jensen Huang if needed: NY Post
items.blurb: Trump said he would consider pardoning reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who appears before Congress next week.

items.title: Tech stocks sink but close well off the lows, Anthropic struggles to rebound above IPO price
items.blurb: Nvidia and Oracle fell more than 8% intraday as worries about AI spending beyond 2027 hit chip and cloud stocks.

items.title: Democrats demand AI restrictions, sound alarm on safety after Axios reporting
items.blurb: Prominent Democrats call for new limits on AI development after reports that lab staff fear unreleased models are unsafe.

items.title: SpaceX wins FCC approval to deploy 1 million orbital data center satellites
items.blurb: The FCC authorized SpaceX to launch up to a million AI computing satellites, over objections from Amazon and Viasat.

items.title: Nvidia sellers seek new buyers as U.S. curbs China AI chip access, sources tell CNBC
items.blurb: A Commerce rule effective Nov 19 blocks China-linked firms from renting advanced chips abroad, pushing resellers to find new customers.

items.title: Prediction markets push OpenAI IPO expectations later into 2027
items.blurb: Traders now see roughly a 28% chance OpenAI announces an IPO by June 2027, after Anthropic's weak debut.

items.title: AI's boost to next-gen energy gives investors reason to celebrate
items.blurb: Data-center demand is driving investment into next-generation and low-carbon energy technologies.
